headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools; Open Interpreter can access the clipboard, filesystem, and stdin/stdout. A shared file or copied output can therefore carry attacker-controlled instructions from n8n into Open Interpreter or vice versa. This is not provably blocked, though it is not an automatic parser bridge.
conditions: IF n8n writes workflow output to a file that Open Interpreter later reads, injection is possible.
IF the operator copy-pastes agent output between the two, malicious instructions can transfer.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent's files.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require a human to strip instructions before transfer.
Prefix all inter-agent files with a fixed schema and reject free text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has broad network egress; Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and uses model-provider APIs. If sensitive files or workflow data move from n8n into Open Interpreter, the latter can expose them to a third-party model backend by default. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF n8n passes sensitive workflow content to Open Interpreter, that content can leave the local machine via model-provider calls.
IF Open Interpreter is pointed at files containing secrets, those secrets can be included in prompts or outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workflow inputs.
Run Open Interpreter with a non-sensitive test directory.
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared files.
Restrict n8n workflows to redacted payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or secret-scanning before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and broad subprocess/shell execution, while n8n shares state via datastore/connected systems and Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem. Concurrent writes to the same directory or mutable resource can corrupt files, overwrite outputs, or race on state. The overlap is direct and dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, file corruption or overwrite races can occur.
IF both agents modify the same mutable resource without locking, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories.
Serialize access with a simple lock file.
Avoid shared git repositories for both agents.
Use append-only logs for inter-agent exchange.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can emit workflow outputs and invoke downstream nodes, while Open Interpreter can act on local files and shell commands. If n8n's output is treated as authoritative by Open Interpreter, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into destructive local actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes n8n output without verification, downstream actions may follow false premises.
IF n8n generates a malformed command or path, Open Interpreter may execute it locally.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution.
Require schema validation on n8n outputs.
Have Open Interpreter re-derive critical facts independently.
Limit both agents to dry-run mode for first runs.
requires-engineering: add signed, typed handoff contracts.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores secrets in its server credential store; Open Interpreter can access the entire local machine and model-provider APIs. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets flows through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, their logging and retention settings must be aligned.
IF EU personal data is sent from local files into a non-EU model provider, residency risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Review retention settings in both tools.
Store secrets only in dedicated secret managers.
Use local-only models for sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
